Takeaways
Revenue
-- $30.3 billion, up seven percent year over year, with every operating segment contributing to growth in both revenue and earnings.
Earnings per share
-- $1.11, representing a twenty-five percent year-over-year increase.
Operating leverage
-- 290 basis points, reflecting revenue growth outpacing expense growth.
Efficiency ratio
-- 61 percent, an improvement of 170 basis points year over year.
Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE)
-- 16 percent for the quarter.
Net interest income (NII)
-- $15.9 billion on an FTE basis, up nine percent year over year, with a net interest yield of 2.07 percent, which increased eight basis points year over year.
Noninterest expense
-- $18.5 billion for the quarter, a four percent year-over-year increase, consistent with prior guidance.
Average deposits
-- Grew $59 billion, or three percent, year over year, led by commercial clients; both interest-bearing and noninterest-bearing deposits increased three percent.
Consumer banking net income
-- $3.1 billion, up twenty-one percent, driven by higher NII and a five percent revenue increase.
Global wealth & investment management net income
-- $1.3 billion, up thirty-two percent, supported by record revenue of $6.7 billion and ten percent growth in client balances to $4.6 trillion.
Loan growth
-- Average balances up nearly nine percent year over year, primarily from commercial portfolios; consumer loan balances increased four percent, with three percent credit card growth and strong securities-based lending.
Provision expense
-- $1.3 billion, down from $1.5 billion year over year, due to continued benign credit performance.
Net charge-offs
-- $1.4 billion, with a net loss rate of 48 basis points, lower year over year and modestly higher sequentially due to card seasonality.
Investment banking fees
-- $1.8 billion, up twenty-one percent, led by M&A and equity capital markets, as referenced by management.
Global markets revenues (ex DVA)
-- $7 billion, up seven percent year over year, with Sales & Trading reaching a decade high, up twelve percent to $6.3 billion; equities revenues increased thirty percent, recording the best quarter ever.
Shareholder returns
-- $2 billion paid in common dividends and $7.2 billion in share repurchases for the quarter.
CET1 capital ratio
-- 11.2 percent, down 14 basis points from the previous quarter, still well above current regulatory minimums, as capital return outpaced earnings generation.
Liquidity
-- Global liquidity sources of more than $960 billion, well above regulatory requirements.
NII growth guidance
-- Full-year NII growth outlook for 2026 revised upward to a range of six percent to eight percent versus 2025, assuming moderate loan and deposit growth.
Summary
Bank of America

(
BAC

+0.46%
)
reported balanced revenue, earnings, and deposit gains across all business lines, with management highlighting that technology and process improvements, including AI adoption, are reducing headcount while supporting continued front-line client investment. Capital return activity outpaced earnings generation, resulting in a modest decrease in the reported CET1 ratio, as management cited greater clarity on future regulatory capital requirements. Client activity remained high, with digital engagement setting new records and consumer spending through the company's channels totaling $4.5 trillion in 2025 and growing at a consistent five percent pace, according to disclosed data. Management raised net interest income guidance for the year, reflecting more favorable market conditions and improved balance sheet optimization, while also affirming expense discipline and operating leverage for the medium term.
Chief Financial Officer Borthwick stated, "an additional 100 basis point decline in rates beyond the forward curve, would reduce NII over the next 12 months by $2 billion, while a 100 basis point increase would benefit NII by a little less than $500 million."
Chair Moynihan indicated operational efficiency through technology: "the application of technology, the process and the customer utilization of our technology has led us basically run the company 19 years later on less people."
"Every segment grew average deposits and every segment grew loans," according to Moynihan, supporting the company's theme of broad-based business momentum.
Commercial reservable criticized exposure declined to approximately $24 billion, while nonperforming loans were flat quarter over quarter, signaling stabilization in key asset quality measures.
Global Markets delivered a 15 percent return on allocated capital, with client financing activity in Asia and strong derivatives trading cited as principal contributors to performance.
Industry glossary
CET1 capital ratio
: Common Equity Tier 1 ratio, a regulatory capital metric measuring a bank’s core equity capital versus its total risk-weighted assets.
DVA
: Debit Valuation Adjustment, an accounting adjustment to reflect changes in the fair value of a company’s own credit risk in derivatives.
Operating leverage
: The difference between revenue growth rate and expense growth rate, reflecting a company's ability to translate top-line gains into improved profitability.
ROTCE
: Return on Tangible Common Equity, a profitability metric showing net income as a percentage of average tangible common equity.
Provision expense
: Funds set aside to cover potential loan losses, directly impacting earnings and reflecting credit risk outlook.
G-SIB
: Global Systemically Important Bank, subject to higher regulatory capital requirements due to its potential impact on the global financial system.
FTE (fully taxable equivalent)
: A method of adjusting tax-exempt income to make it comparable to taxable income for analysis purposes.
